output.reason: A 71-year-old with a fall this morning, severe right hip pain and inability to bear weight has a likely hip fracture requiring immediate emergency imaging and treatment, and she cannot safely move or self-transport.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now. A fall with severe hip pain and being unable to put weight on that leg strongly suggests a broken hip, which needs emergency X-rays and treatment today. Stay still where you are, do not try to stand or walk on that leg, and do not drive yourself. If you develop chest pain, fainting or confusion while waiting, tell the dispatcher.
differential: Proximal femur (hip) fracture from ground-level fall
Hip dislocation or pelvic/pubic ramus fracture

redFlags.concern: Inability to bear weight after fall
redFlags.quote: I can't put any weight on that leg.
I fell in the kitchen this morning and my right hip hurts badly.

citations.claim: Hip/groin pain with inability to bear weight after a ground-level fall in an older adult is the classic hip fracture presentation.
citations.limitation: Compiled ED synthesis; classic-presentation description, not a triage rule.

citations.claim: Fractures can be occult on plain films when a patient cannot bear weight, so in-person imaging pathways are needed rather than remote assessment.
citations.limitation: Describes imaging strategy after ED evaluation; no imaging has been done here.
